author_bio: Kanika Solanki is currently a student at the University of Delhi, pursuing her bachelor's in journalism. She has a keen interest in photography and graphic designing & has previously interned as a content writer. The quest for gaining new information and experiences keeps her going.
content:
The identifying trait of autocratic politics, the most elementary means of taking control of a people, is cutting out their resources. And the first of these to go, perhaps even before dignity & survival, is thought. And the capacity to hold on to it.

Kanika Solanki is currently a student at the University of Delhi, pursuing her bachelor's in journalism. She has a keen interest in photography and graphic designing & has previously interned as a content writer. The quest for gaining new information and experiences keeps her going.
excerpt: A photo essay on autocratic politics and the suppression of thought, the first resource any authoritarian strips from a people is not dignity but the capacity for independent thinking. Photographs and text by Kanika Solanki, journalism student at the University of Delhi.

related.excerpt: A seven-panel illustrated essay by journalist and activist Firaaq, written from the experience of his own arrests at the India Gate and JNU Long March protests, on Sharjeel Imam's return to Tihar jail, and what it means to witness the state's appetite for detention from inside a cell. Illustrated by Mouli Sharma.
related.title: Ek Waqt ki Namaaz

related.excerpt: A photo essay from International Women's Day, 8th March 2026, at Jantar Mantar, where women from six to sixty gathered to protest the BJP government's neglect of women's safety and welfare, express solidarity with the women of Palestine and Iran, and raise demands for dignity, health, and work.
related.title: Bengal Remembers: Sengar, Epstein, and RG Kar's Legacy on International Women's Day in 2026

related.excerpt: A photo essay from the 52nd New Delhi World Book Fair and its unlikely neighbour, Nakshatra, the trade fair for astrology, tarot, and all things con, held side by side at Pragati Maidan. On the strange coexistence of faith and reason, superstition and literature, in one of the capital's great annual public spaces.
related.title: अंधविश्वास और अन्य बकवास

related.excerpt: A re-examination of Julius Caesar beyond Shakespeare's romantic portrayal, the general who conquered the Gallic tribes by exploiting their internal divisions, triggered a civil war, and earned enough enemies to be stabbed twenty-three times by his own colleagues.
related.title: The First Dictator

related.excerpt: Drawing on Ram Chandra Guha's comparison of Mussolini's Italy and Modi's India, this long read examines how democracies slide into authoritarianism not through sudden rupture but through incremental normalisation, and what the historical record of regimes that did end tells us about the one we are in.
related.title: Boiled Frogs: A Case Study of One of Global Politics' Most Haunting Autocratic Takeovers & the Quiet Revelations it Makes About Modern Democracy
